title: Hearing George Baquet with Robichaux and deciding to play clarinet
summary: Hearing George Baquet on clarinet with Robichaux's band made him decide to learn clarinet; he recalls the band's members and Robichaux's violin.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Nobody. See? I just picked it up. In fact, sir, when the John Road show came to Thibodeau, George Backe was playing Clownet, you know. George who? Backe.

And of course I had been playing violin and violin, but I didn't play the piano. So I, he was playing, he was playing that song about, that song, you know. And it went all through me, you know. I just got a trill out of that, you know, the sound, you know, that harmony from that clarinet, you know. And it stayed with me. See? I said, the last thing I'm going to do, I said, I'm going to learn how to play clarinet.
When was that you heard, George Backe?
That was about 19, 19, 19, 19, somewhere around that time. I imagine it was long in that time. The Robichaux's band came up?
Yeah, Robichaux, yeah, yeah. He played like a clarinet solo on that, huh?
Well, no, he was playing the band, the whole band. The whole band. The whole band.
Remember who else was in the band then when you heard them?

Yeah, Backe and Robichaux and Contrat I think was playing drums. And he had William from Homer, Louisiana. Yeah, yeah, yeah. I think James Williams, I think his name was James Williams. How did Robichaux play on violin?
Was he really good? Was he left handed? Was that? He was left handed. Was he really a good? Oh yeah, oh yeah, it is.

At that time, you know, he was just recognized, you know. And the music, we was playing two, four time music at that time, you know. But now it's what you call, you know, it's even more two, four time music.
